title: Graph Data Condensation via Self-expressive Graph Structure Reconstruction

problem.claim: Large-scale graph training creates storage and training-time costs, motivating condensation into a smaller synthetic graph that preserves information needed for downstream GNN training.

gap.claim: Existing methods either optimize node features alone or independently learn node features and graph structure, without explicitly using the original graph structure or constructing an interpretable synthetic structure.

contributions.claim: Introduces GCSR, a framework for graph data condensation via self-expressive graph structure reconstruction.
Explicitly incorporates the original graph structure into the condensation process.
Reconstructs an interpretable self-expressive graph structure to capture interdependencies between condensed nodes.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish GCSR by explicitly incorporating the original graph structure and reconstructing an interpretable self-expressive structure for condensed nodes.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments and comprehensive analysis across diverse GNN models and datasets.
The authors report that the code is available in a public repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Large-scale graph training incurs storage and time costs.
Graph data condensation aims to produce a much smaller synthetic graph while preserving essential downstream training information.
Existing approaches do not explicitly exploit original graph structure or produce interpretable synthetic structure.
GCSR addresses the gap through original-structure incorporation and self-expressive graph reconstruction.
The authors report experiments across diverse GNN models and datasets and provide code.

source_observation.claim: The method uses original graph structure and reconstructs an interpretable self-expressive structure for condensed nodes.

interpretation.claim: Preserving and exposing relational structure may improve the usefulness and interpretability of condensed graph representations.

application.claim: When designing graph condensation methods, consider jointly preserving source-graph structure and making synthetic relationships interpretable.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which datasets, GNN models, or application settings benefit most from this design.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the condensation algorithm, objective functions, or reconstruction procedure.
The abstract does not report quantitative results, baselines, dataset names, or computational costs.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported efficacy.
